dataQuality.limitations: This is not a complete national outbreak line list and must not be interpreted as proof that no other events exist.
principles: unknown is not treated as zero
surveillance updates are not labelled as outbreaks unless the source confirms an outbreak
country-level programme information is kept separate from event-level disease reports

events.summary: WOAH endorsed Zimbabwe's official control programme for dog-mediated rabies in 2026. The endorsement recognises the national control programme; it does not mean Zimbabwe is free from rabies.
events.notes: WOAH listed Zimbabwe among Members with an endorsed official control programme for dog-mediated rabies according to Resolution No. 27 of the 93rd General Session in May 2026.

events.summary: WOAH's evaluation of Zimbabwe's dog-mediated rabies control programme reported multi-year surveillance data, including 1,625 animal samples tested between 2018 and 2024, with a declining trend in the percentage of positive samples. Zimbabwe reported case definitions for human and animal rabies and use of IDSR/DHIS2 for related human surveillance and dog-bite reporting.
events.sourceTitle: Ad hoc Group evaluation of official control programmes for dog-mediated rabies
events.notes: The source discusses historical surveillance and programme performance. It is not a 2026 outbreak count.

events.summary: FAO's Sub-Saharan Africa HPAI situation update reported a multisectoral HPAI situational analysis in Zimbabwe and routine government surveillance in large commercial poultry farms, with samples submitted quarterly. The update also noted gaps in surveillance capacity and practices.
events.sourceOrganisation: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO)
events.notes: The cited FAO update does not state that Zimbabwe had a confirmed HPAI outbreak in this item; therefore the feed records this as surveillance intelligence, not a confirmed outbreak.
